title: Experimental Design Anatomy
description: A benchmark research question whose key phrases are draggable chips, sorted by the learner into research question, independent variable, dependent variable, and controlled variables, with hints on mismatch and three worked examples from different domains.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Benchmarking
Research Methods

educational.topic: Decomposing a benchmark question into its experimental variables
learningObjectives: Classify phrases of a research question by experimental role
Distinguish an independent variable from a dependent variable
Construct a benchmark suite from a well-formed question
prerequisites: An experiment compares outcomes under changed conditions
Familiarity with FFT size, window type, and sample rate

controls.label: Phrase chip
controls.purpose: Move a phrase from the sentence into a category box

controls.label: Check my answers
controls.purpose: Score the placements and give a hint on the first mismatch

controls.label: Try a new example
controls.purpose: Cycle to a question from a different application domain

controls.label: Clear this one
controls.purpose: Return every phrase to the sentence

simulationModel.modelType: Drag-and-drop classification over an inline sentence flow with three worked examples
equations: correct = count of chips where placement equals the answer key
each example has exactly one research question, one independent variable, one dependent variable and three controlled variables
assumptions: Every question is written in the form: does A change B, holding C, D and E fixed
Exactly one independent variable per question, which is what makes the design interpretable
limitations: Does not cover factorial designs with more than one independent variable
Does not address replication, variance, or sample size

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Direct manipulation with category-level hints rather than answers, repeated across unrelated domains to force transfer
keyQuestions: Which phrase is the thing you change, and which is the thing you read off?
How many benchmark runs does this question require?
commonMisconceptions: Confusing the independent and dependent variables
Treating the research question as a variable
Leaving controlled variables unstated because they seem obvious
assessmentOpportunities: Write a new research question in the same form and list the runs it implies
Explain why a second independent variable makes a result uninterpretable
